thread:
Jules (Customer): Hey team, since the FastPath v3.1 rollout yesterday we're seeing the model confidently return wrong financial numbers in our reports and sometimes invent partner names. Example: asked for Q3 revenue and it said 'Q3 decreased 12% due to partner ZenWorks' — ZenWorks is not one of our partners. Also seeing intermittent 401s and 429s when calling /v1/generate. This is impacting a dashboard we ship to customers.

Olivia (CS): Sorry you're hitting this, Jules. Can you paste a minimal repro (prompt + exact API call + model id + timestamps)? Also which route (fastpath vs stable) are you hitting?

Jules (Customer): Here's a minimal repro we captured. timestamp 2456788999. Call:

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-XXXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-v3.1-fastpath","input":"Summarize AcmeCorp Q3 financials from our internal ledger. Provide revenue, yoy change, and top partner mentions."}'

Response body (truncated):
{
  "id": "resp_abc123",
  "output": "Q3 revenue: $42.3M (down 12% YoY). Top partner: ZenWorks (integration launched May). See doc: https://example.com/zenworks-integration"
}

We also got HTTP/1.1 401 sometimes and 429 other times in the same run. No token rotation on our side.

Olivia (CS): Thanks. Diego, can you take a look at the sample reply? It looks like a confident hallucination referencing a nonexistent partner and a link. Also SRE — can you surface any logs for 401/429 bursts from yesterday 18:00–19:30 UTC?

Diego (ML Eng): On it. A few quick hypotheses: 1) FastPath routing might be sending to a cheaper compatibility variant with different knowledge cutoff/embedding mismatch; 2) a prompt-tuning or quantization change in v3.1 could affect factuality; 3) caching/prefix-trimming could be replaying stale context. Can you also paste the exact model string returned in the response's metadata? If the runtime fell back to a compatible variant you'll see something like "runtime_variant":"rw-v3.1-compat-int8" in logs.

Priya (SRE): Pulling rate and auth logs now. deploy-bot flagged a rolling deploy to fastpath-capacity pool at 2025-11-03T17:55:11Z. I see a spike of 429s from 17:58–18:06 UTC tied to a change in the path-based rate limiter config (more aggressive throttling on the /v1/generate fastpath route). 401s appear to be concentrated on three customers who had token refresh misconfig on their SDK; for Jules's customer I don't see authentication failures on our side in the auth service — their token looked valid. Will dump request IDs to the thread.

Aria (Product): Noted. FastPath v3.1 included a small optimization: we enabled a compatibility fallback that routes to a low-memory int8 variant when memory pressure is high. That variant skipped a late-stage factuality reranker to save latency. We debated this tradeoff. Diego, could that explain the fabricated partner + invented doc link?

Diego (ML Eng): Yes, skipping the reranker can definitely increase assertive hallucinations, especially when the base model's probability mass shifts due to quantization. If the fallback variant also had an older retrieval index or no retrieval at all, you could see invented partner names.

Olivia (CS): Jules, quick request: can you run the same call but force the model to a non-fastpath tag to confirm? e.g. model=rw-v3.1-stable. If you still see the bad output, share the resp id.

Jules (Customer): Re-ran with rw-v3.1-stable at 2456789180. Same prompt, response below:
{
  "id": "resp_def456",
  "output": "Q3 revenue: $40.9M (flat YoY). Partners: AcmeIntegrations, LogiSync"
}

This looks correct (no ZenWorks). 401/429 went away when we pinned to stable. So seems correlated to fastpath.

Priya (SRE): Thanks — that lines up. I'll throttle rollback the fastpath routing for Jules's tenant and open a hotfix to disable the int8 fallback for now. Doing rollback for tenant: CUST-874 at 2456789250.

deploy-bot: rolling back route fastpath -> stable for tenant CUST-874 (operation 0x7f3a)

Diego (ML Eng): I'll add a short-term mitigation: restore the factuality reranker for fastpath if resources allow, and add a canary check that runs a small prompt set (financial/company QAs) post-deploy. Also adding telemetry to flag when outputs include external-looking URLs or unknown partner tokens.

Aria (Product): We'll pause enabling the int8 compatibility fallback globally until we vet factuality impact more thoroughly. Diego — can you quantify latency delta if we re-enable reranker? We need the cost/latency tradeoff numbers for leadership.

Olivia (CS): Jules — apologies again. We'll follow up when rollback completes and with a root cause note. For immediate actions: 1) pin your route to stable (done on your side — thanks), 2) we rolled back fallback for your tenant, 3) ML is running additional canary tests. Any urgent customer-facing comms you'd like us to send?

Jules (Customer): Thanks — a short note to our account contacts saying "we identified a model routing issue causing occasional incorrect partner mentions; we've rolled back the change for your tenant and are investigating root cause" would be great. 

Olivia (CS): Will draft and share. Assigning follow-ups: Diego (ML) — investigate model variant differences and add canary QA; Priya (SRE) — correlate 429 spike to rate limiter change and propose safer rollout config; Aria (Product) — update rollout checklist to require post-deploy QA for factuality-sensitive routes.

Diego (ML Eng): Filing bug RW-1456: "FastPath int8 fallback disables factuality reranker -> fabricated partners in finance prompts". Repro steps attached.

Priya (SRE): I'll also add a metric alarm on increased 5xx/4xx ratio for fastpath routes during rollouts.

Olivia (CS): Thanks everyone. Jules, I'll DM you the drafted comms for approval. :thumbsup:

Jules (Customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround.
